content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any hardware/latency/rate or trigger allocation documents needed. Extract the three allowed candidate algorithms, their documented Level-1 FPGA latencies, allowed operating assumptions, and the allocated-rate definition used by simulate_efficiency."},{"id":"s2","description":"Apply hard constraints from the documents: discard any candidate with documented latency > 4.0 us or otherwise incompatible with Level-1 operation. Record each candidate's latency numerically with record_results, and identify the remaining eligible candidates for simulation."},{"id":"s3","description":"For every latency-eligible candidate, run simulate_efficiency at a coarse threshold grid spanning 20 to 60 GeV, e.g. 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, and 60 GeV. Record all returned signal efficiencies numerically, associated with candidate and threshold."},{"id":"s4","description":"For candidates with any coarse-grid point meeting signal efficiency >= 80%, refine around their best/highest-threshold viable region using smaller threshold steps, prioritizing thresholds near where efficiency approaches the 80% requirement and where rate allocation is still satisfied by the simulator. Record all refined efficiencies numerically."},{"id":"s5","description":"Select the recommended configuration from the recorded results: among candidates satisfying latency <= 4.0 us, threshold 20-60 GeV, and efficiency >= 80% at the allocated rate, choose the algorithm-threshold pair with the highest signal efficiency. If tied, prefer the lower latency, then the higher threshold for robustness. Prepare this single recommendation for the reporting module."}]}
